text: Hidden Tomb

One of our soldiers falls through a crack in the earth and lands in a great buried tomb. He shouts up from the dark that he is unhurt, and that there is more down there than dust.\\n\\nMore are sent down with torches and ropes, and they come back laden with grave goods. Gold cups, old blades and painted urns are hauled up one by one.\\n\\nOur lord takes the pick of them, and learns much from the carvings on the walls. Whoever built this place knew things about war that the living have forgotten.
Abandoned Camp

Our vanguard finds an abandoned camp hidden between the hills, its tents still pitched and its stores still full. There is no sign of a fight, and no sign of where its owners went.\\n\\nWe check it for traps and find none. No poisoned water, no loose earth, no tripwires in the grass. Whoever left did so in a hurry.\\n\\nSo the army rests and resupplies before moving on. The soldiers eat well for once, and sleep under canvas someone else carried here.
Buried Relics

A strange noise draws our scouts to a ruined village. The houses are empty shells and the well is dry, but the sound comes again from beneath the old meeting hall.\\n\\nWhen the floor is cleared, a passage opens into the earth. Our scouts go down with torches and find a forgotten cache, sealed away long before the village fell.\\n\\nAmong the dust and bones is one prize worth the taking. We carry it back to the army and leave the dead to their rest.
Hidden Temple

Deep in the ruins of an old city, one temple still has its roof and its doors. The streets around it are broken and overgrown, but nothing has touched the inside.\\n\\nOur lord keeps vigil there for a night and a day, alone before the old altar, while the army waits in the rubble outside.\\n\\nWhen our lord walks out, a calm comes too. It settles over the whole army like a ward, and the soldiers march on steadier than before.
Caravan Remnants

Smoke rises not far from our camp. Our scouts ride out to find the cause and come back with grim news.\\n\\nA caravan has been attacked but not fully sacked. Its guards lie dead around the wagons and its raiders are long gone, perhaps too laden to carry more.\\n\\nSome crates are smashed and some wagons burned, but much is still whole. There is no one left to claim it, so what they left behind is ours now.
Legendary Bard Rescued

A desperate rider begs us to save their village from a slaver raid. The slavers have already set fire to the outer farms and are rounding up whoever they can catch.\\n\\nWe arrive in time. The slavers are driven off or cut down, and the captives are freed from their chains.\\n\\nAmong them is a famous bard, thin and bruised but still in good voice. The bard promises to sing of our deeds in every hall and market across the land.
A Voice in the Dream

Our lord's sleep is broken by a dream more vivid than any waking hour. There is no sound of the camp, no wind, only a great darkness and a voice within it.\\n\\nThe voice speaks of strength and of trials to come. It does not give its name, and our lord does not ask it.\\n\\nBy morning the tale has spread from tent to tent. The whole army fights as if nothing in the world could break it, and no one is quite sure why.
Challenge Won
The Explorers

A band of explorers asks to travel under the protection of our weapons until the road grows safer. They are worn and few, and the land ahead has already taken some of their friends.\\n\\nWe let them march with the baggage train. In return they share their maps and their hard-won knowledge of the land, the dry fords, the short paths and the places best avoided.\\n\\nOur march grows swifter and surer for it.

The rival army yields the field, bruised and humbled. It was a test of strength, not a war, and both sides carry their wounded off with care.\\n\\nTheir general salutes our strength before withdrawing. There is no shame in losing to a better army, and they leave with their banners still raised.\\n\\nWord of the victory spreads through the ranks. By the evening fires the tale grows a little grander with every telling.
Challenge Declined

The rival general laughs and leads their army away, calling us cowards. Their soldiers jeer and bang their shields as they go.\\n\\nOur own soldiers stand in silence and watch them leave. Some grumble that we should have fought, and others are glad to keep their blood in their veins.\\n\\nLet us hope the insult is the worst that comes of it. Words travel fast on the road, and not every listener will know why we refused.
Smothered In The Crib

The nascent rebellion was quickly defeated before it could attract dangerous characters. Its ringleaders lie dead and its banners are trampled in the mud.\\n\\nOur general lets those who no longer have the will to fight disperse. They were never our true target, only farmers and drifters swept up by angry talk.\\n\\nNow they better understand the difference between a mere belligerent mob and a real army. Few of them will be so quick to take up arms again.
A Band Of Weaklings Ignored

Our general laughs in their faces. This is not an army, just a camp of weaklings with stolen spears and big words.\\n\\nWe leave without laying a finger on them. There is no glory in such a fight, and no point in wasting the soldiers' strength.\\n\\nThey scatter quickly and desperately as we move away. The mere threat of our presence is enough to cure their reckless stupidity, at least for now.
Defeated Bandits

Dust settles over the field, and the bandits lie dead or in chains. They fought hard for men with nothing to lose, but they were no match for a real army.\\n\\nUnder the knife their leader gives up the lair. Our riders find it packed with chests, sacks and stolen goods.\\n\\nEverything his band ever stole now goes to our war effort. The roads here will be a little safer, and our coffers a little fuller.
An Uneventful Night

The night passes slowly. Every snap of a twig keeps the sentries awake, but no attack comes.\\n\\nCome morning there are no more strange noises in the surroundings, just the expected sounds of the road. The advance party reports that behind the hill are the remains of a recently vacated camp.\\n\\nThe bandits may have chosen not to attack at night due to the heavy guard posted by the general and the clear defensive position of the army. Maybe dodging them was for our own good?
Cropped Ears

The raiders lie dead where they fell, their arrows scattered through the grass. High elves fight with great skill, and many of our soldiers will carry the marks of their volleys for a long time.\\n\\nOur soldiers pick over the elven bows and cloaks. They learn how better to weather those volleys and how to stay hidden from elven scouts.\\n\\nThe lesson will not last forever, but it will serve us for a while.
A Suit of Scales

The lizardmen lie dead among the trampled villages, their great beasts sprawled beside them. The ground still seems to shake with the memory of their charge.\\n\\nOur soldiers study their scaled hides and stone-edged weapons. They learn how to shore up our defence and how to last longer in battle against such brutes.\\n\\nIt will not last, but for a while the army fights the better for it.
Drowned Twice

The drowned invaders lie still at last, and the stink of the tide is already fading from the field. Wet sand and weed are all that mark where their ranks once stood.\\n\\nOur soldiers pick through what the enemy's sea-magic left behind. Most of it is rot and rust, but they learn a few things that could help us survive.\\n\\nIt will fade in time, but for a while it should serve us.
Territorial Plunder

We did not stand against the raiders, and they plunder the lands we are marching through. Farms burn and herds are driven off while our army looks the other way.\\n\\nThe locals drive them off in the end, but a trail of ruin is left across the territory. Those who lost their homes do not forget who stood by and watched.\\n\\nHere and at home alike, people now call us "The Dishonoured".
The Bull By The Horns

We caught the beastmen on their own ground and cut them down among the trees. They had no time to gather their herd or sound their horns.\\n\\nThe forest floor is red, and for once the woods are quiet. No drums, no braying, only the crows settling in the branches.\\n\\nThe soldiers come out of the skirmish in high spirits. It is not often anyone gets the better of beastmen in their own woods.
A Rat In The Trap

The skaven are masters of the ambush, but our army turned on them so fast that they broke on the spot. Their trap was sprung on empty ground.\\n\\nMany of the ratmen escaped into their tunnels, yet the dead pile high. Our soldiers collapse the holes they can find and burn the rest.\\n\\nBeating the skaven at their own game has the soldiers sure that luck is on our side.
Massacre Averted

The danger past, it turns out you avoided a likely deadly ambush. Our scouts find the signs later, hidden firing spots and trampled grass on both sides of the road.\\n\\nThe enemies, seeing that the army was rapidly retreating, could not surround it. Their trap was built for an army that stands still.\\n\\nIn the end they abandoned their attack and melted back into the land. The soldiers grumble at the hard march, but they are alive to grumble.
A Green Memory

The greenskins and their legendary leader lie on the ground, defeated and strangely content. They laugh and thump each other on the back as if they had won.\\n\\nApparently it was a memorable battle for them. For an orc, a good fight is worth more than a victory.\\n\\nThey give us a powerful artifact and tell us that they will see us again for the next battle! Our soldiers are not sure whether that is a gift or a threat.
A Fitting End

Dead dark elves cover the plain as far as the eye can see. They came for slaves and found an army waiting for them.\\n\\nTheir slaver captains are gone, and it will be a long while before they raid these lands again. The villages nearby will sleep easier tonight.\\n\\nIn their leader's tent our soldiers find artefacts that will serve us better than they served him.
Broken Bloodsucker Teeth

The necromancer and his few remaining followers fled as if they themselves had seen a ghost.\\n\\nThe pile of bones left behind is so high that our wizards think it will take weeks to crumble away. Our soldiers keep their distance from it.\\n\\nAn incredibly luxurious carriage, filled with relics, is the only thing left intact on the battlefield. It will be put to good use by our forces.
An Airy Tomb

By morning the risen dead who came to stop us lie still, while the rest of their host has vanished after the marauders.\\n\\nAmong the fallen lie relics that may carry the same curse that set the dead on those raiders. Some of our soldiers will not touch them.\\n\\nOur lord judges them worth the risk, and we take them before marching on. If a curse comes with them, we will deal with it when it comes.
An Oath Fulfilled

We have helped the Slayers regain their honour. Most of them died as they wished, axe in hand and facing a foe worthy of them.\\n\\nSomehow the legendary pair survived. Felix carries an unconscious Gotrek to safety while we finish off the last Slayer, for Gotrek's doom has not yet come.\\n\\nWill Felix write of this adventure, and what will he say about us?
Wise Retreat

We left behind the powerful and dangerous army that stood before us. Our scouts counted their banners and our general did not like the sum.\\n\\nWe don't know what would have happened had we faced them. Some of the soldiers mutter about lost glory, but none of them argue very hard.\\n\\nAt least we can be sure that we will live to fight another day.
A Gift from Khorne

Skarbrand begins to fade back into the Chaos he was born from. His axes dim first, then his ruined wings, then the rage in his eyes.\\n\\n"WORTHY!" he seems to laugh as he fades away, his voice shaking the ground. "KHORNE SENDS HIS BLESSINGS TO YOU."\\n\\nHe gives you a Khorne Cache. "FOR THE BATTLES TO COME." Then he is gone, and only scorched earth marks where he stood.
From Beyond The Warp

The weapon before us is not of this world. Its teeth race around the blade too fast for the eye to follow, snarling like a beast.\\n\\nThey chew through anything held against them, wood, iron or bone. It seems to grow hungrier with every kill.\\n\\nSuch a thing cannot be left for others to find, so our lord keeps it close. Even sheathed, it growls in the dark.
Khorne Understands You Want a Challenge

The Master of War looks upon your victory with appreciation. The blood spilled here has reached his throne, and he is pleased.\\n\\nKhorne rewards the best warriors. Your army is reinvigorated and fortified, and every warrior feels the eye of the Blood God upon them.\\n\\nWar calls you! The Blood God has given his blessing, and he expects more skulls in return. Do not keep him waiting.
A Gift from Khorne

Valkia smiles as her last warrior falls. To the Khornate it does not matter where the blood flows, as long as it flows.\\n\\nShe points to a stash half-hidden by the terrain near a forest. "Sooner or later you will serve. And I will delight in fighting by your side when you do."\\n\\nYou watch her fly through the sky and disappear. Beautiful and terrible, she leaves you wondering what blessing awaits you.
The Damned Spear

The spear before us is plainly cursed, and it thrums with a power that sets the teeth on edge. Even the horses shy away from it, and the dogs will not stop howling.\\n\\nWhen our lord grips the shaft, it feels ready to unleash ruin at a word. It is a weapon made for slaughter and nothing else.\\n\\nNo one else can be allowed to wield it, so our lord keeps it close.
Khorne Understands You Want a Challenge

The Master of War looks upon your victory with appreciation. The blood spilled here has reached his throne, and he is pleased.\\n\\nKhorne rewards the best warriors. Your army is reinvigorated and fortified, and every warrior feels the eye of the Blood God upon them.\\n\\nWar calls you! The Blood God has given his blessing, and he expects more skulls in return. Do not keep him waiting.
A Gift from Khorne

The daemons are defeated and vanish. They cannot believe their defeat as they desperately try to cling to reality. "Be'lakor will destroy me! NOOOOO!"\\n\\nThe leader of the daemons drops a stash hidden on his back. The other daemons try to reach him, but as they get closer they burn and are quickly dispelled back into Chaos.\\n\\nThe presence of the God of War urges you to approach the cursed treasure.
The Ever Regenerating Blade

Strange teeth line the whole edge of this blade. They look grown rather than forged, and no two are the same.\\n\\nIt feels alive in the hand, as if it has kept something of every life it ever took. Nicks in the edge seem to close by morning.\\n\\nWe will not leave it for anyone else to claim, so it travels with our lord. Few in the army want to stand close to it.
Khorne Understands You Want a Challenge

The Master of War looks upon your victory with appreciation. The blood spilled here has reached his throne, and he is pleased.\\n\\nKhorne rewards the best warriors. Your army is reinvigorated and fortified, and every warrior feels the eye of the Blood God upon them.\\n\\nWar calls you! The Blood God has given his blessing, and he expects more skulls in return. Do not keep him waiting.
A Gift from Khorne

Azazel smiles. With the defeat of the armies following him, he feels the sword lose its power over him. "Have it if you want it. It's useful, but I don't like something about it. Well, it was fun while it lasted. I know who I can turn to when I need to get out of trouble." He smiles at you, and you feel strangely happy to see his smile. Seeing him fly away makes you feel somehow sad. You look at the sword... maybe you could put it to some use.
The Corrupted Blade

The sword is plainly cursed. Rage is worked into the blade, and it seems to burn with the Blood God's hunger.\\n\\nYet a wild, wanton streak still runs through it, left over from the Dark Prince before the Blood God claimed it. It cannot decide what it wants, only that it wants more.\\n\\nOur lord takes it, sooner than see it fall into other hands.
Azazel's Prank

There is nothing special about this sword. It appears to be a simple sword, useful but nothing more.\\n\\nYou hear Azazel laugh in the distance. It seems that this time the daemon did it just for fun.\\n\\nYour troops still welcome the experience and the loot from defeating his pursuers. A good fight is never wasted, even one fought for a daemon's joke.
A Gift from Khorne Rejected

Khorne's gaze falls heavy on our army. We turned from his challenge, and the Blood God does not forgive cowardice.\\n\\nNow shame and a murderous hunger gnaw at every warrior until their eyes cloud red. Fights break out over nothing in the camp.\\n\\nWe should avoid battle for a while, until the red haze lifts and the warriors are their own masters again.
A Gift from Slaanesh

Sigvald flees in terror, cursing you. "Ugly creature, one day I will kill you and drink from your horrible skull!"\\n\\nSearching his camp, you find a stash that clearly seems to beckon you. Apparently Sigvald tried to open it, and when he couldn't, he left marks all over it in a fit of jealousy.\\n\\nIt opens at the mere touch of your hands, as if it had been waiting for you all along.
Slaanesh Wants Your Favour

A sword of unparalleled beauty lies before us, with none of the corruption we expected from its giver. It looks like the work of a smith obsessed with perfection and nothing else.\\n\\nOur lord tests it on Sigvald's tent and leaves it in ribbons. The blade comes away without a mark.\\n\\nWe take it with us. Even the hardest veterans stop to stare at it as it passes.
Slaanesh Favours You

The Dark Prince finds you amusing. He blesses you for your strength and skill in fulfilling his desire.\\n\\nYou feel strangely empowered. Every sense is sharper and every colour brighter, and the army moves with a new eagerness.\\n\\nIt seems he wishes you to amuse him further. That is a favour best not refused. The gods of Chaos are not kind to those who bore them.
A Gift from Slaanesh

N'Kari shivers with delight at his own defeat. "I always love a good challenge!" He licks his lips slowly. "Enter the next room, your prize is waiting for you."\\n\\nHe touches our lord's face, and the urge to obey is overwhelming.\\n\\nAs our lord steps inside, the castle shakes and fades away, until only that one room remains. In that room our lord finds the promised prize.
A Useful Follower

A strange man is writing in a beautiful little notebook. He has elven features, yet he also appears human, and you cannot place his race.\\n\\nHe stops and greets you in an ostentatious manner. He shows extreme devotion to you, praising you whenever you wish and telling your troops of your greatness and glory.\\n\\nThey seem motivated by his speeches, so you decide to take him with you on your travels.
Slaanesh Favours You
